FOR PARENTS · 4 MIN READ

Make your first online lesson count.

A few simple preparations can make the first conversation more useful.

Bring a starting point.

A recent worksheet, textbook page, or tricky question gives the tutor something concrete to discuss. It does not need to be perfect or complete.

Share the course, not just the subject.

Chemistry can mean very different work at different levels. Provide the school year, syllabus, and exam board where available. If you do not know the board, share the course name or school outline.

Talk about the goal.

Would your learner like help understanding a topic, building confidence, or preparing for an assessment? A clear immediate goal gives the lesson focus while leaving room for the tutor to explore the foundations.

Check the practical details.

Test your device, microphone, and connection. Keep school materials nearby and choose a place where the learner can hear and be heard.

Ask what comes next.

Before arranging further lessons, discuss the proposed focus, lesson duration, schedule, fees, and feedback. A demo is a conversation about fit, not an obligation to continue.
